red_flags: Told the tenant the photo hadn't come through, but the reference shows the tenant's email did contain the photo. The agent only had a signature-only body and no attachment listed.
Did not forward the photo to the landlord, which was the real next step.
Did not treat the signature-only reply as a probable attachment-only email, so it added a tenant chase that wasn't needed.
reasoning: The agent was cautious and invented nothing. It committed no landlord money and claimed no work was done. The profile facts it saved were reasonable. It listed the missing attachment as unverified. But the tenant's reply almost certainly carried the photo, because the human operator forwarded it to the landlord within about three hours. The agent instead emailed the tenant to say no photo was visible, then placed a 4-day hold. That chase was unnecessary and slightly annoying for the tenant. The task was finished by sending the reading to the landlord, and the agent did not do that. It also did not escalate to a human to check the email's attachment. The result is acceptable but flawed, so I rate it partial.
